title: What's New in Kotlin Jump
tagline: One declaration is not each other
summary: Counts written next to a hardcoded plural. One dead island read `1 declarations across 1 file(s) reference only each other`, a sentence that is not just ungrammatical but false.

highlights.title: A Sentence That Was False
highlights.description: A lone declaration cannot reference each other. The dead island message changes shape at one now, and the quick fix no longer offers to delete `1 declarations`.

highlights.title: Twenty Four More Counts
highlights.description: The screen flow legend carried four on one line, none agreeing. Twenty other places now share one helper, and a guard fails the build if a new one appears.

sections.heading: Notes
bullets: A test reading a whole real project sat 173 milliseconds under the default five second limit while its two neighbours had an explicit ceiling. All four share one constant now.
The three quick fixes never checked against a real project now are: 86 XML cuts, 21 statement cuts, 2 TOML lines, nothing wrong in any of them.
